Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

balancesample 0.0.0.9000

  • First draft of the package: balanced_vfold_cv(), balanced_initial_split(), balance_check(), and four balancing methods ("anticlust", "twinning", "rerandomize", "interaction").

  • Workflows with a postprocessor that must be trained (for example, a tailor calibration) now work with tune::fit_resamples() and tune::tune_grid() on balanced folds, and with tune::last_fit() on balanced training/testing splits. The inner calibration split uses the same balance columns, exact strata, groups, method, and options as the outer split, without twinning’s strategy option. This needs rsample 1.3.1 or later.

  • labels() of repeated folds now combines the repeat and fold IDs, as it does for rsample::vfold_cv().

  • New “Get started” article that walks through a full tidymodels workflow.

  • balanced_vfold_cv() and balanced_initial_split() now reject unknown arguments. If you pass strata, the error tells you to use exact.

  • New balanced_initial_validation_split() makes a training/validation/testing split. All three sets are balanced in one pass. It works with rsample::validation_set(), tune::tune_grid(), and tune::last_fit().

  • balance_check() now works on three-way splits, including those from rsample::initial_validation_split(). It compares the validation and testing sets each with the training set.

  • method = "twinning" can now make sets of unequal size from whole numbers of similar parts.

  • With method = "twinning", balanced_initial_split() now checks that prop is a fraction twinning can make before it rounds the set sizes, so the check no longer depends on the data size. Before, a prop such as 0.7 could pass on small data because of rounding. Write prop as a fraction, such as 2 / 3, not 0.67. A value within a relative 1e-8 of a fraction counts as that fraction.

  • rsample::internal_calibration_split() on a twinning three-way split now uses the nearest training share that twinning can make (for example 5/6 instead of 14/17). Before, such shares gave a warning and an empty calibration set. That still happens when the training set can’t be split, for example when it has fewer than two groups.

Developed by Jeffrey M. Girard.
